text:
Aisha: Heads-up — planning a new EKS GPU nodepool in us-east4 for batch inference (mixed H100/A10g). Preflight checklist: quotas, NAT egress IPs, ENI limits, and CA tuning. Need input on networking constraints.
Rafael: +1. What's the expected pod density? ENI limits usually bite if we use larger instance counts per AZ.
Aisha: Target is 8 nodes per AZ initially, autoscale up to 50 on demand. Pods will use sidecars for metrics and a caching layer — roughly 6 pods/node for busy periods.
Jun: If you hit ENI nic-per-instance limits, we should prefer instances with higher ipv4-per-instance or move to CNI v2. Also consider using prefix delegation or smaller podENI if allowed.
Marta: Also watch NAT GW elastic IP quota for the VPC — we're provisioning a shared NAT with 3x HA IPs, but bursting into 50 nodes might require additional egress IPs depending on SNAT port exhaustion.
Aisha: Good call. I opened a cloud quota ticket last week but no resolution yet. Want a mitigation plan in case quota isn't approved fast.
Rafael: Mitigations: 1) Use NAT Gateway per AZ with SNAT port optimization; 2) Use NAT instances (cheaper but less managed) with auto-scaling groups and connectivity checks; 3) Move egress to private endpoints where possible to reduce SNAT footprint.
Product-ML: For batch inference we can also route heavy telemetry to a private ingest endpoint to avoid public egress. That reduces SNAT usage by ~40% in our sims.
Jun: Also consider using multiple smaller private subnets and split workloads across them to spread ENI and SNAT port utilization.
Aisha: For node sizing: we're debating 4x H100 vs 8x A10g mix. Cost-wise A10g cheaper but higher node counts -> more ENIs. H100 reduces node count but cost per hour is higher. Need ops preference.
Marta: From a networking POV fewer but larger nodes are easier (less ENI count, fewer IPs, less NAT pressure). But remember GPU memory and concurrency tradeoffs.
Rafael: Autoscaler config proposals: --scale-down-unneeded-time=10m, --max-node-provision-time=20m, and PodPriority for batch vs realtime. For GPU pools, use NodeGroup taints: `gpu=true:NoSchedule` and tolerations only for inference pods.
Aisha: Draft YAML for node group snippet:
```yaml
apiVersion: eksctl.io/v1alpha5
kind: ClusterConfig
nodeGroups:
  - name: gpu-hybrid-us-east4
    instanceType: a10g.48x
    desiredCapacity: 8
    minSize: 2
    maxSize: 50
    taints:
      - key: "gpu"
        value: "true"
        effect: "NO_SCHEDULE"
    tags:
      role: gpu
```
Jun: That looks fine; change `instanceType` to a list if you want mixed SKUs to allow fallback. Also add `labels` for affinity: `workload: inference`.
Aisha: We also need a graceful fallback policy when quotas are constrained — route lower-priority jobs to hosted API or a cheap CPU pool. Any thought on automatic fallbacks?
Rafael: Implement a router service that checks nodepool capacity via the cluster API + a policy engine. If pool unavailable, rewrite job queue to target `cpu-burst` queue and add a header for degraded mode. Keep it simple first.
SRE-Oncall: From reliability side: add a node-provisioning alert if scale-up hasn't completed in 15m and pod pending count > 20. Also alert on SNAT port exhaustion signs (TCP throughput drops, SYN retries).
infra-bot: Deployment event: Created terraform plan for VPC change (natgw+route-table). Plan ID: plan-20260308-42.
Aisha: Thanks infra-bot. Action items: 1) I will request extra EIP quota with cloud support and include expected SNAT port calculations. 2) Rafael to prototype fallback router logic. 3) Jun to validate ENI/pod density with CNI settings. 4) Marta to run egress cost sim.
Marta: I'll run sims and post numbers (SNAT EIP count vs monthly cost) by EOD.
Rafael: I'll throw together a small router PoC and a knob to fall back to `cpu-burst` queue. ETA 2 days.
Jun: I'll simulate pod-to-node mappings and share max safe pods/node for each instance SKU by tomorrow.
Aisha: If quota doesn't come through, fallback plan is: reduce desiredCapacity, prefer H100s to reduce node count, and rate-limit outbound egress to avoid SNAT storms.
Product-ML: One more ask — can we pin some inference workloads to a dedicated subset of nodes (nodeAffinity + podAntiAffinity) so we don't evict realtime jobs during scale events?
Rafael: Yes, use requiredDuringSchedulingIgnoredDuringExecution affinity on label `realtime=true` and set scale-down-protection annotation for those pods.
Aisha: Ok let's reconvene after the sims and PoC. Thanks everyone :thumbsup:
SRE-Oncall: Noted, will add a runbook entry for NAT exhaustion and fallback steps.
infra-bot: Reminder: Cloud quota request 12345 updated to "Pending - URGENT".
